open_points.subject: MigrationClosure identity across store histories
open_points.text: “two records of ‘the migration succeeded at instant T’ would mean the same thing” conflicts with “an instance that restores a store from before the import may import again, and that history then holds its own closure”
open_points.question: Are closures created by successful imports in different store histories distinct history-scoped facts, even when their recorded facts are equal, or are they the same value wherever those facts are equal?
options: Each store history owns a distinct closure occurrence, requiring store-history scope to distinguish it
Equal closure facts denote the same value across histories; only their placement in different stores differs
open_points.default_guess: Treat each closure as scoped to its store history, without adding a globally comparable closure identity.

open_points.subject: MigrationClosure uniqueness used by AuditEntry
open_points.text: M09 says “the migration closure is unique in the instance and has no other identity”, while M10 now says “at most one per store history” and that “an instance that restores a store from before the import may import again”
open_points.question: Is the closure unique only in the current store history, or must audit subjects distinguish multiple closures that can arise over the lifetime of one Registry instance after restores?
options: Replace instance-wide uniqueness with uniqueness in the current store history; the file digest remains the audit subject
Keep instance-wide uniqueness and give repeated post-restore imports a way to refer to distinct closures
Treat each restored store as a new instance for model identity purposes
open_points.default_guess: Read M09’s uniqueness as uniqueness within the current store history and keep the accepted file digest as the audit subject.

open_points.subject: MigrationClosure lifecycle after restoring a backup that already contains it
open_points.text: “None; absent, then present for the rest of the store’s history” does not say how this applies when “the restored store begins its own history from the backup” and that backup already contains the closure
open_points.question: Does a restored store history inherit the backed-up history, including the original absent-to-present transition, or does it begin at restore with MigrationClosure already present as initial state?
options: The new history includes the backed-up prefix, so the original import remains the transition that created the closure
The new history starts at restoration with the closure as an inherited initial fact
Restoration creates a new MigrationClosure from the backed-up facts
open_points.default_guess: Treat the backed-up prefix as part of the restored store’s history, preserving the original import as the closure’s creation.
